passages.text: Now the Spirit expressly states that in later times some will abandon the faith to follow deceitful spirits and the teachings of demons, influenced by the hypocrisy of liars, whose consciences are seared with a hot iron.
passages.sermon:
The Holy Spirit speaks clearly.
The Spirit says what will happen in the future.
In later times, some people will leave the Christian faith.
These people will follow spirits that deceive.
They will accept teachings that come from demons.
Liars will influence them.
These liars act with hypocrisy.
Their consciences are seared and no longer feel right or wrong.
passages.original: Τὸ δὲ πνεῦμα ῥητῶς λέγει ὅτι ἐν ὑστέροις καιροῖς ἀποστήσονταί τινες τῆς πίστεως προσέχοντες πνεύμασιν πλάνοις καὶ διδασκαλίαις δαιμονίων ἐν ὑποκρίσει ψευδολόγων κεκαυστηριασμένων τὴν ἰδίαν συνείδησιν

passages.text: They will prohibit marriage and require abstinence from certain foods that God has created to be received with thanksgiving by those who believe and know the truth.
passages.sermon:
Some people will prohibit marriage.
Some people will require abstinence from certain foods.
God created these foods.
God created these foods to be received with thanksgiving.
Believers receive these foods with thanksgiving.
Those who know the truth receive these foods with thanksgiving.
passages.original: κωλυόντων γαμεῖν ἀπέχεσθαι βρωμάτων ἃ ὁ Θεὸς ἔκτισεν εἰς μετάλημψιν μετὰ εὐχαριστίας τοῖς πιστοῖς καὶ ἐπεγνωκόσι τὴν ἀλήθειαν

passages.text: For every creation of God is good, and nothing that is received with thanksgiving should be rejected, because it is sanctified by the word of God and prayer.
passages.sermon:
God creates everything.
Every creation of God is good.
We should not reject anything that God has made.
If we receive something with thanksgiving, we should accept it.
The word of God makes things holy.
Prayer also makes things holy.
God’s word and prayer sanctify what we receive with thanks.
passages.original: ὅτι πᾶν κτίσμα Θεοῦ καλόν καὶ οὐδὲν ἀπόβλητον μετὰ εὐχαριστίας λαμβανόμενον ἁγιάζεται γὰρ διὰ λόγου Θεοῦ καὶ ἐντεύξεως

passages.text: By pointing out these things to the brothers, you will be a good servant of Christ Jesus, nourished by the words of faith and sound instruction that you have followed.
passages.sermon:
You are a servant of Christ Jesus.
You teach and care for other believers.
You point out these important truths to them.
You follow the words of faith.
You follow sound teaching.
These words and teachings nourish you.
You have learned and obeyed these teachings.
passages.original: Ταῦτα ὑποτιθέμενος τοῖς ἀδελφοῖς καλὸς ἔσῃ διάκονος Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ ἐντρεφόμενος τοῖς λόγοις τῆς πίστεως καὶ τῆς καλῆς διδασκαλίας ᾗ παρηκολούθηκας

passages.text: But reject irreverent, silly myths. Instead, train yourself for godliness.
passages.sermon:
Reject irreverent myths.
Reject silly myths.
Do not accept these stories.
Train yourself for godliness.
Practice living in a way that pleases God.
Focus on becoming more like God wants you to be.
Do not waste time on false stories.
Work to grow in faith and holiness.
passages.original: Τοὺς δὲ βεβήλους καὶ γραώδεις μύθους παραιτοῦ γύμναζε δὲ σεαυτὸν πρὸς εὐσέβειαν

passages.text: For physical exercise is of limited value, but godliness is valuable in every way, holding promise for the present life and for the one to come.
passages.sermon:
Physical exercise helps only a little.
Godliness helps in every way.
Godliness brings benefits now.
Godliness brings benefits in the future life.
passages.original: ἡ γὰρ σωματικὴ γυμνασία πρὸς ὀλίγον ἐστὶν ὠφέλιμος ἡ δὲ εὐσέβεια πρὸς πάντα ὠφέλιμός ἐστιν ἐπαγγελίαν ἔχουσα ζωῆς τῆς νῦν καὶ τῆς μελλούσης

passages.text: This is a trustworthy saying, worthy of full acceptance.
passages.sermon: This saying is trustworthy.\r\nEveryone should fully accept it.
passages.original: πιστὸς ὁ λόγος καὶ πάσης ἀποδοχῆς ἄξιος

passages.text: To this end we labor and strive, because we have set our hope on the living God, who is the Savior of everyone, and especially of those who believe.
passages.sermon:
Paul writes to Timothy.
Paul and Timothy work hard.
They struggle for a purpose.
They do this because they hope in God.
God is alive.
God saves all people.
God especially saves those who believe.
passages.original: Εἰς τοῦτο γὰρ κοπιῶμεν καὶ ἀγωνιζόμεθα ὅτι ἠλπίκαμεν ἐπὶ Θεῷ ζῶντι ὅς ἐστιν Σωτὴρ πάντων ἀνθρώπων μάλιστα πιστῶν

passages.sermon:
Paul speaks to Timothy, a young Christian leader.
Paul gives Timothy instructions.
Paul says, "Command these things."
Paul also says, "Teach these things."

passages.text: Let no one despise your youth, but set an example for the believers in speech, in conduct, in love, in faith, in purity.
passages.sermon:
Timothy is a young Christian leader.
\r\nDo not let anyone look down on you because you are young.
\r\nBe an example for other believers.
\r\nShow this example in your words.
\r\nShow this example in your actions.
\r\nShow this example in your love.
\r\nShow this example in your faith.
\r\nShow this example in your purity.
passages.original: Μηδείς σου τῆς νεότητος καταφρονείτω ἀλλὰ τύπος γίνου τῶν πιστῶν ἐν λόγῳ ἐν ἀναστροφῇ ἐν ἀγάπῃ ἐν πίστει ἐν ἁγνείᾳ

passages.text: Until I come, devote yourself to the public reading of Scripture, to exhortation, and to teaching.
passages.sermon:
Paul writes to Timothy.
Paul is an apostle and elder.
Timothy is a young church leader.
Paul gives Timothy instructions.
Paul says, "Until I come, devote yourself to the public reading of Scripture."
Paul says, "Devote yourself to exhortation."
Paul says, "Devote yourself to teaching."
passages.original: ἕως ἔρχομαι πρόσεχε τῇ ἀναγνώσει τῇ παρακλήσει τῇ διδασκαλίᾳ

passages.text: Do not neglect the gift that is in you, which was given you through the prophecy spoken over you at the laying on of the hands of the elders.
passages.sermon:
Timothy, you have a special gift inside you.
God gave you this gift.
The elders spoke a prophecy about you.
They laid their hands on you when they did this.
Do not neglect this gift.
Use your gift faithfully.
passages.original: Μὴ ἀμέλει τοῦ ἐν σοὶ χαρίσματος ὃ ἐδόθη σοι διὰ προφητείας μετὰ ἐπιθέσεως τῶν χειρῶν τοῦ πρεσβυτερίου

passages.text: Be diligent in these matters and absorbed in them, so that your progress will be evident to all.
passages.sermon:
Paul writes to Timothy.
Paul gives Timothy instructions for ministry.
Paul tells Timothy to be diligent in these matters.
Paul tells Timothy to focus on these things.
Paul wants Timothy to be absorbed in them.
Paul says this will make Timothy’s progress clear.
Everyone will see Timothy’s progress.
passages.original: ταῦτα μελέτα ἐν τούτοις ἴσθι ἵνα σου ἡ προκοπὴ φανερὰ ᾖ πᾶσιν

passages.text: Pay close attention to your life and to your teaching. Persevere in these things, for by so doing you will save both yourself and those who hear you.
passages.sermon:
Pay close attention to your life.
Pay close attention to your teaching.
Continue steadfastly in both your life and your teaching.
If you do this, you will save yourself.
If you do this, you will save those who listen to you.
passages.original: ἔπεχε σεαυτῷ καὶ τῇ διδασκαλίᾳ ἐπίμενε αὐτοῖς τοῦτο γὰρ ποιῶν καὶ σεαυτὸν σώσεις καὶ τοὺς ἀκούοντάς σου
